output.summary: A deciduous broad-leaved tree whose native origin is not stated, it is common along Himalayan lowlands from Kashmir to western Nepal. It has abundant white flowers and forms a rounded canopy. Its seeds are dried and ground into bitter flour, with the saponins thoroughly washed out before cooking.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are dried and ground; bitter saponins are thoroughly washed out before the flour is used in chapatis, halwa or porridge.
